source.description: owner/repo, a git URL, or the literal "builtin"

official.description: Published by the verified first-party marketplace; this does not mean Core-owned.

type.description: App (ships a Companion UI surface, or bundles other apps) vs plugin (tools/agents/channels/policies). Preferred over deriving app-ness from a Companion runnable.

hasCompanion.description: True when this item ships a Companion UI surface (i.e. an app). Sets type=app when `type` is omitted.

bundles.description: Ids of separate plugins this item ships as a logical bundle (installed/uninstalled together). Rendered as "Includes these apps".

icon.description: Icon-primitive glyph id: an Iconify `prefix:name` (e.g. `lucide:ghost`) or a bare Hugeicons name. Distinct from `iconUrl` (a raster logo).

iconDither.description: Dithered-gradient background painted behind the icon glyph on the card, and (absent an explicit `banner`) behind the detail hero. `from` is a palette colour name (green|blue|purple|pink|orange|red|grey) or a hue number; `to` defaults to transparent; `direction` is up|down|left|right. camelCase, matching the key Core deserialises and the key the manifest itself uses — this was documented as `icon_dither` and nothing ever read that.

from.description: Palette colour name or hue number

hidden.description: Hide this listing from the store without removing it from the index. Absent means visible, so an older client that predates the field simply shows everything — the safe direction for a flag whose job is to remove things. This is the LIVE control point: flipping it here hides the listing for every already-shipped client on its next catalog fetch, with no release.

stability.description: How finished this listing is: `alpha`, `beta`, `rc`, … Absent or `stable` means finished and renders no badge. Free-form on purpose — an unrecognised tier renders verbatim rather than being dropped, so a new tier needs no client release.

surfaces.description: Host surfaces this listing runs on (desktop, island, mobile, web, extension, cli, core, gateway), with any explicitly-unsupported surface already filtered out. Absent means NOT DECLARED, which the store shows as "runs everywhere"; it is never emitted as `[]`, which would read as "runs nowhere".
